connects_to.relationship: renewable power supply (corporate power purchase agreement and UK renewable energy supply management)

contracts.signal: Shell's 20-F (Renewables and Energy Solutions): in May 2025 Shell signed a new Corporate Power Purchase Agreement (CPPA) with Google, which extends the lifespan of the NoordzeeWind offshore wind farm in the Netherlands.

Shell's 20-F: in September 2025 Google selected Shell Energy Europe Limited as its renewable energy supply manager in the UK, under the USA-based technology company's Carbon-Free Energy supply model to reach its goal of running entirely on clean energy by 2030; Shell says the role leverages its trading and battery capabilities to support Google's decarbonisation goals.

quarterly_data.signal: Shell's 20-F full-year 2025 results: income for the period $18.1 billion (2024: $16.5 billion), Adjusted Earnings $18.5 billion (2024: $23.7 billion), cash flow from operating activities $42.9 billion (2024: $54.7 billion), free cash flow $26.1 billion (2024: $39.5 billion) and cash capital expenditure $20.9 billion (2024: $21.1 billion). Revenue was $266,886 million (2024: $284,312 million), including oil products $114,660 million, crude oil $35,711 million, LNG $33,467 million, natural gas and NGL $22,825 million, power $12,260 million and lubricants $11,544 million. Oil and gas production available for sale was 2,800 thousand boe/d (2024: 2,836) and ROACE 9.4% (2024: 11.3%). Total spend on goods and services was around $40 billion from suppliers around the world (2024: $41 billion).
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 income $18.1 billion; Adjusted Earnings $18.5 billion; CFFO $42.9 billion; free cash flow $26.1 billion; cash capex $20.9 billion; revenue $266,886 million (vs $284,312 million); LNG revenue $33,467 million; power revenue $12,260 million; production 2,800 thousand boe/d

quarterly_data.signal: Shell's 20-F capital plan: cash capital expenditure is planned within $20--22 billion per year between 2025 and 2028. For 2026 Shell expects cash capex of around $12-14 billion for Integrated Gas and Upstream ($14.0 billion in 2025) and around $8 billion for Marketing, Chemicals and Products, and Renewables and Energy Solutions ($6.9 billion in 2025); by segment, around $6 billion in Integrated Gas, around $7 billion in Upstream, $2-3 billion in Marketing and around $3 billion in Chemicals and Products. 2025 cash capex by segment was Integrated Gas $4,689 million, Upstream $9,316 million, Marketing $1,862 million, Chemicals and Products $3,063 million and Renewables and Energy Solutions $1,866 million; $2.0 billion of the 2025 total went to low-carbon energy solutions.
quarterly_data.figure: cash capex $20--22 billion per year 2025-2028; 2026: Integrated Gas and Upstream around $12-14 billion, downstream and renewables around $8 billion; 2025 Upstream $9,316 million; Integrated Gas $4,689 million; Renewables and Energy Solutions $1,866 million

quarterly_data.signal: Integrated Gas per the 20-F: 2025 LNG liquefaction volumes were 28.4 million tonnes (2024: 29.1) and LNG sales volumes 72.9 million tonnes (2024: 65.8). Shell calls itself the world's leading publicly listed supplier of LNG, with around 44 million tonnes of equity capacity, and says its Integrated Gas portfolio services nearly a fifth of global LNG demand. The first LNG shipment left LNG Canada (Shell interest 40%; two trains with collective capacity of 14 million tonnes a year) on June 30, 2025. LNG plants under construction at December 31, 2025 include Nigeria LNG Train 7 (7.6 mtpa), QatarEnergy LNG NFE(2) (8.0 mtpa) and NFS(2) (6.0 mtpa), and Ruwais LNG (9.6 mtpa). In October 2025 Shell took an FID on the HI gas project under OML 144 after concluding a gas supply agreement under which gas from the HI field will be supplied to Nigeria LNG Ltd (NLNG). Shell's 2025 LNG Outlook forecasts global LNG demand to rise by around 60% by 2040.
quarterly_data.figure: LNG liquefaction 28.4 million tonnes; LNG sales 72.9 million tonnes (vs 65.8); around 44 million tonnes equity LNG capacity; LNG Canada 14 million tonnes a year, 40% interest; LNG demand +60% by 2040

quarterly_data.signal: Power and Renewables and Energy Solutions per the 20-F: 2025 external power sales were 290 terawatt hours (2024: 306) and sales of pipeline gas to end-use customers 626 terawatt hours (2024: 652). Renewable power generation capacity in operation (Shell interest) was 4.2 gigawatts (2024: 3.4) with 1.9 gigawatts in development (2024: 4.0). In January 2025 Shell acquired RISEC Holdings and its 609 MW two-unit combined-cycle gas turbine power plant in the USA. Shell says it shifted the Power business from capital-intensive renewables development to a capital-light, trading-led, asset-backed model, selling its interests in SouthCoast Wind Energy LLC and other renewables positions, withdrawing from Atlantic Shores Offshore Wind and exiting two floating wind projects in Scotland, and is targeting returns of around 10% across the Power portfolio by 2030. In November 2025 Shell Energy Europe Limited signed power purchase agreements in Germany with Nordsee One GmbH and Solarkraftwerk Halenbeck-Rohlsdorf I/II GmbH to secure a significant proportion of the renewable electricity for the 100 MW REFHYNE II hydrogen electrolyser (operations scheduled to begin in 2027). In June 2025 Shell Energy Europe and Vodafone Procure & Connect launched a battery storage pilot in which Vodafone accesses part of the operational benefits of Shell's 100 MW, 3-hour battery site in Hampshire.
quarterly_data.figure: external power sales 290 TWh (vs 306); pipeline gas to end-use customers 626 TWh; renewable capacity in operation 4.2 GW (vs 3.4); in development 1.9 GW; RISEC 609 MW; Power returns target around 10% by 2030; REFHYNE II 100 MW

quarterly_data.signal: Downstream and low-carbon projects per the 20-F: 2025 refinery utilisation was 92% (2024: 85%) and chemicals manufacturing plant utilisation 78% (2024: 76%). At Rheinland, the Wesseling base oils plant is expected to produce approximately 300,000 tonnes of Group III base oils a year when complete in 2028. Holland Hydrogen I is expected to start commissioning towards the end of 2026 with production ramp-up in 2027. Northern Lights (Shell interest 33.3%) plans to scale transport and storage capacity from 1.5 million tonnes to at least 5 million tonnes of CO2 a year by 2028, after Stockholm Exergi signed for up to 900,000 tonnes of biogenic CO2 annually for 15 years; the Polaris carbon capture facility at Scotford is designed to capture around 650,000 tonnes of CO2 a year. Public EV charge points reached almost 88,000 at end-2025 (2024: almost 73,000). On March 9, 2026 Shell agreed to sell Jiffy Lubricants International to an affiliate of Monomoy Capital Partners and entered into a long-term lubricants supply agreement with Monomoy; closing is expected in the second half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: refinery utilisation 92% (vs 85%); chemicals utilisation 78%; approximately 300,000 tonnes Group III base oils (2028); Northern Lights 1.5 to at least 5 million tonnes CO2 a year by 2028; Stockholm Exergi up to 900,000 tonnes a year for 15 years; almost 88,000 EV charge points

quarterly_data.signal: Upstream per the 20-F: 2025 production available for sale was 1,828 thousand boe/d (2024: 1,831), with liquids at 1,365 thousand b/d. Shell says it has delivered 25% of the more than 1 million boe/d of new production promised by 2030. In the Gulf of America, 2025 production was 377 kboe/d; Whale, which started in January 2025 with nameplate output of 100,000 boe/d, is now expected to peak at 117,000 boe/d in 2026, and Dover is expected to produce up to 14,000 boe/d at peak. The Orca (formerly Gato do Mato) project in Brazil is designed for peak production of up to 120,000 b/d, with the FPSO to be built in China and Japan, installed in 2028 and operations expected to begin in 2029. Manatee and Aphrodite in Trinidad and Tobago are expected to start in 2027, with peak capacity of 104,000 boe/d and about 18,400 boe/d respectively.
quarterly_data.figure: Upstream production 1,828 thousand boe/d; Gulf of America 377 kboe/d; Whale peak 117,000 boe/d in 2026; Orca up to 120,000 b/d from 2029; Manatee 104,000 boe/d and Aphrodite about 18,400 boe/d from 2027
